outcomes.original: Filing step: Engage an architect licensed in California with San Francisco restaurant experience to prepare plans for the building permit, DBI review, and the DPH plan check. What to say: The architect must analyze the existing certificate of occupancy to determine whether the project is a Building Code change of occupancy, design egress paths and ADA compliance for 98 seats (at least 50 occupants, so Group A-2), specify the kitchen hood and fire suppression system, and coordinate with a mechanical engineer for the grease interceptor and FOG program compliance. Submit plans to DPH and DBI simultaneously to avoid sequential delays.

outcomes.original: Filing step: File the Conditional Use Authorization application with SF Planning Department, including the architect's plans, a project description stating hours (6 a.m. to midnight), seating (98), no alcohol service, and a good-neighbor operations plan. What to say: Frame the application as a continuation of the established restaurant use at this address (cite the 2012 approvals) expanding to serve the West Portal neighborhood with a full-service dining experience. Commit to the expected conditions: maintaining sidewalks within one block, soundproofing the space to SF Noise Ordinance standards, installing odor control equipment per DPH approval, keeping trash on-site except during disposal service, and appointing a community liaison. Emphasize that the concept serves food without alcohol, closes by midnight (well within the 6 a.m.–2 a.m. principally permitted window), and will be owner-operated with direct neighborhood accountability.
outcomes.note: The cited application is from 36 West Portal Ave (not the report address), dated 2018-2019 (not 2012), and limited hours to 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. (not midnight). The permitted hours window is not in the records.

outcomes.original: Filing step: Attend the Planning Commission hearing on the Conditional Use Authorization and present the application, respond to Commissioner questions, and accept the recommended conditions. What to say: Testify that Elena's Restaurant continues the restaurant use approved at this address in 2012, that the concept serves the neighborhood with a full-service dining experience without alcohol, that the hours (6 a.m. to midnight) are within the principally permitted window and consistent with nearby restaurants, and that the operator commits to all standard eating-and-drinking conditions. If Commissioners ask about the 3,995 sq ft size or storefront merger, confirm that the architect's plans show full ADA compliance, adequate egress for 98 seats, and that the design respects the West Portal streetscape. Accept any hours, noise, trash or liaison conditions the Commission imposes.
outcomes.note: Record is for different address (36 West Portal, not 243) and different restaurant (Kaleifornia, not Elena's); approved hours were 6am-8pm, not 6am-midnight.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the CUA is approved and the 30-day appeal period expires, file the building permit application with DBI, including the architect's plans, the approved CUA Motion, and the DPH plan check approval. What to say: The building permit application routes to Planning for zoning compliance review; attach the approved CUA Motion to confirm the use is authorized. The plans must show the kitchen hood and fire suppression system, the grease interceptor sized per SFPUC FOG program requirements, ADA-compliant restrooms and paths of travel, and egress capacity for the occupant load. Request that DBI route the permit to the Fire Department for hood and Place of Assembly review (98 seats, so occupant load over 50).

outcomes.original: Filing step: Submit the DPH plan check application for the new food facility, with two sets of scaled drawings, interior and exterior photos, the menu, and the equipment list. What to say: The plan check application should describe limited cooking (per the concept description), specify all food prep surfaces, hand sinks, three-compartment sinks, hot water capacity, and finishes (sealed, smooth, easily cleanable). State that a certified food safety manager will be on staff before the pre-opening inspection (California Health Code §113947.1 requires one per facility). Schedule a pre-final inspection at 80% construction complete and a final inspection, booking each with the DPH plan reviewer at least two weeks in advance.

outcomes.original: Filing step: After the building permit is finaled and the DPH pre-opening inspection passes, apply for the Health Permit to Operate with the Business Account Number, Location ID, federal EIN, and the food safety manager certificate. What to say: The Health Permit to Operate application (FY2026–27: $470 application fee, $0 annual license fee for restaurants through 2028) is submitted online at least one month before opening and is issued after the final inspection confirms the facility matches the approved plans and a certified food safety manager is on staff. Ensure all employees obtain California Food Handler Cards within 30 days of hire (Health Code §113948). Set up workers' compensation insurance and organics recycling service (SB 1383) before opening.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 120 to 300 days. Estimated government cost: $3,100 to $18,000. Notes: This is the time to approval for the Conditional Use Authorization, building permit, DPH plan check and health permit when those approvals are granted. The Conditional Use Authorization is the critical path: 4 to 10 months from filing to Planning Commission hearing and 30-day appeal period. Building permit and DPH plan check run in parallel after the CUA is approved (14–120 days for building, 21–60 days for DPH plan check). Cost range covers the CUA application fee ($3,100–$15,000 depending on construction cost, with possible First Year Free waiver for new storefronts), building permit fees ($800–$15,000 as a percentage of construction valuation), DPH plan check ($828–$2,500 for a new restaurant, flat fee 8 hours at $276/hr), health permit to operate ($470 application), Fire Place of Assembly permit ($446), and FOG program registration ($0–$500). State and federal registrations (EIN, entity formation, seller's permit, EDD) add $70–$150 and take 1–14 days but are not counted in the approval timeline. Music licensing (ASCAP, BMI) adds $600–$5,000 annually and takes 1–7 days. The timeline assumes no appeal of the CUA, no discretionary review of the building permit, and no failed inspections; any of those add 2 to 6 months.
